text:
A: Hello? You on?
B: Yeah. Hiya. Joanne. St Helens.
A: Tracey. Dagenham.
B: Another Tracey.
A: Yeah, there's two of us. You had the other one, then?
B: First one I had, yeah.
A: What d'you reckon?
B: She was alright. Bit much, to be honest. Told me you can't pour from an empty cup.
A: Ha! She told me she'd pick me up in her Evoque. From Dagenham.
B: Did she.
A: She did. Anyway. I shouldn't. What d'you do?
B: Look after me mum. She's got dementia. So I'm not working.
A: Oh. Sorry. That's hard. My mum's not great neither, her heart. I worry about her all the time, d'you know what I mean. Lie there at night going over it.
B: I don't sleep either. Three, four in the morning, I'm just lying there.
A: Same. Then I'm knackered on shift. I clean offices, evenings.
B: I've done cleaning. Primary school. Didn't last long.
A: It's alright. Nobody about.
B: My husband's out all hours an' all. Delivery driver.
A: You're joking. So's mine. Multi-drop.
B: Same. What's he called?
A: Gary.
B: Mine's Gary.
A: Shut up. Honestly?
B: Honestly. Gary.
A: That's mad. Does yours moan about the van?
B: All the time. His back, the van, the traffic. Before Christmas I don't see him.
A: Ours got clamped once outside a block of flats in Ilford. Two hundred quid. He was on the phone to the council shouting for an hour, I had to go in the other room.
B: Gary'd do that.
A: They're all the same, Garys.
B: Maybe. Have you got kids?
A: No. We tried. Didn't happen.
B: No. Us neither.
A: Yeah... so. Erm. You got any pets?
B: Cat. Mabel. She's sick on the settee every other day.
A: I've got Duchess. Staffy. Back legs are going.
B: Is it just you and Gary looking after your mum, then?
A: Pretty much. I ain't spoke to my sister in four years.
B: I barely speak to mine. She's twenty minutes away and I do it all. What happened with yours?
A: My nan's will. It's a long story, d'you know what...
